The BrainLat Project is a comprehensive, open-access neuroimaging dataset developed by the Latin American Brain Health Institute (BrainLat) to advance research on neurodegenerative diseases within underrepresented populations. It encompasses multimodal data from 780 participants across five Latin American countries: Argentina, Chile, Colombia, Mexico, and Peru.​

28andMe is a dense-sampling, multimodal neuroimaging study conducted by the Emily Jacobs Lab at UC Santa Barbara. It aimed to investigate how endogenous fluctuations in sex hormones across a complete menstrual cycle influence brain function and structure.

28andHe is a complementary study to 28andMe, focusing on a male participant to explore diurnal hormone fluctuations and their impact on brain function. Conducted by the same research team, this study provides insights into how daily variations in hormones like testosterone affect neural dynamics.

Abbreviation: The Reading Brain Project L1 Adults
Description: This dataset includes neuroimaging and behavioral data from 52 native English-speaking adults. Participants underwent two sessions involving reading tasks, aiming to explore the neural mechanisms underlying reading in first-language (L1) adults.

Abbreviation: The Reading Brain Project L2 Adults
Description: This dataset comprises data from 56 bilingual adults who are second-language (L2) English readers. It investigates how bilingualism and second-language acquisition influence the neural processes of reading.

A cross-sectional dataset from Southwest University in China, encompassing structural and resting-state fMRI data from 494 healthy adults aged 19 to 80. It serves as a resource for studying brain aging and lifespan-related neural changes. ​

A longitudinal dataset featuring multimodal MRI (structural, diffusion, and resting-state fMRI) and behavioral assessments collected over three and a half years. It includes repeated measures from healthy young adults, facilitating research on brain development and test-retest reliability.

Abbreviation: Japanese Strategic Research Program for the Promotion of Brain Science
Description: A Japanese nationwide initiative providing a multi-site, multi-disorder MRI dataset. It includes resting-state fMRI and structural MRI data from 993 patients across various psychiatric disorders and 1,421 healthy controls, supporting research into brain network markers and cross-site harmonization. ​

A dataset comprising high-resolution structural MRI scans from healthy control participants. It is utilized for studies requiring detailed anatomical brain imaging and serves as a control group in various neuroimaging analyses. ​

This dataset includes low-resolution resting-state fMRI data from 100 healthy individuals. It is designed for assessing the intrinsic organization of the human brain at rest and is suitable for studies focusing on functional connectivity.
